senses.gloss:
(I)--a son born of अप्रवाण (Apruvat-मत्स्य प्।) and ऋची, being born from her thigh. Father of ऋचीक. Jamadagni was his grandson; a मन्त्रकृत् and sage.
1: Br. III. 1. ९५; II. ३२. १०५; ३८. २७; M. १९५. १५-16; वा. ५९. ९६; ६५. ९२.
Sagara who had no son visited his hermitage with his two wives and was blessed for sons. Present at Sagara's अश्वमेध and other sacrifices and taught him the path to salvation;
2: भा. IX. 8. 8 & ३१; Br. III. ३४. 2; ५०. २९-58; ५१. 1-४१; ५२. ३७; ५५. 3; ६३. १२२, १३३-4; वा. ८८. १२३, १३२-4; Vi. IV. 3. २९, ३७.
spoke to Sagara on the mode of worshipping विष्णु;
3: M. १२. ४०; Vi. III. 8. 6-१९.
on वर्ण- धर्म;
4: Vi. III. 8. २०-40.
on आश्रमधर्म;
5: Ib. ch. 9 (whole).
on rituals;
6: Ib. ch. १० (whole).
on the duties of the householder;
7: Ib. chapters ११-12.
on funeral rites;
8: Ib. chapter १३ (whole).
on the श्राद्ध;
9: Ib. chapters १४-16; १७. 1.
pre- [page१-290+ ३८] vented the pregnant queen of बाहु(ka) from committing सती,
१०: भा. IX. 8. 3; Vi. IV. 3. २९-37.
and the posthumous son Sagara brought up in his hermitage to whom he did all सम्स्करस्। Was visited and revisited by परशुराम.
११: Br. III. २१. ३५; २५. ८१; Vi. IV. 3. ३६.
Phalgutanta took refuge near his hermitage;
१२: Br. III. ४७. ७९-87.
extinguished the तालजङ्घ line.
१३: भा. IX. २३. २८.
Came to see परीक्षित् practising प्रायोपवेश।
१४: भा. I. १९. १०.
A description of his hermitage.
१५: Br. III. ५०. ३४-45.
A sage of the स्वारोचिष epoch, and one of the five Pravaras of भार्गव gotra.
१६: M. 9. 8; १९५. २९.

(II)--(सम्वर्तक, वडवामुख: s.v.). Hari took this form of fire and drank the waters of the sea;
1: Br. II. १८. ८०; III. ७२. १७; M. 2. 5; वा. ४७. ७६.
ब्रह्मा fixed him in the वडवामुख ocean; celebrated for और्वीमाया (s.v).
2: M. १२१. ७७; १७५. १८, ५८-72.

--a son of पुरूरवस्, became king; father of नहुष; he was a धार्मिच् king and the sages performed a great sacrifice; the assembly looked like that of Indra when the Gandharvas sang, the Apsaras danced, the sages entered into debates and delivered sermons of all kinds. वा. 2. २३-36.
--used by Maya to dispel the darkness of तामसास्त्र; earned by हिरण्यकशिपु from Aurva in the तारकामय war. M. १७५. २०-71.
